Robot Doctor Vision

AprilTags aren't detected or are unreliable

Missed detections, short range, or wrong distance. Below are the 5 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 6 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Does it detect tags when the robot is still, but not while moving? Park in front of a tag, then drive past it.
  • Does it detect tags up close but not from farther away? Move back from the tag a foot at a time.
  • Are tags detected, but the distance or angle numbers are wrong? Measure the real distance with a tape measure and compare.
  • Does the camera disappear until you power cycle the robot? The camera stops showing up or vision returns nothing until a restart.
  • Do you have a grounding strap and all USB devices in the USB 3.0 port? The grounding strap is a short wire with a resistor from a spare XT30 port to the frame. The Control Hub's USB 3.0 port is the blue one.
  • Is a camera or vision pipeline running during teleop? A VisionPortal, AprilTag processor, or Limelight streaming.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 Motion blur or bad exposure

Auto exposure blurs tags when the robot moves. Short exposure plus high gain keeps tags sharp.

How to fix it 15 min

  1. Set exposure to manual, start very low, and raise gain. FIRST's ConceptAprilTagOptimizeExposure sample walks through it.
  2. Raise exposure only until tags are detected reliably at your real driving distance.
  3. Some webcams do not support manual control. The Logitech C920 supports all of the SDK camera controls.
Manual exposure + gain
ExposureControl exposure = visionPortal.getCameraControl(ExposureControl.class);
exposure.setMode(ExposureControl.Mode.Manual);
exposure.setExposure(6, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS);
GainControl gain = visionPortal.getCameraControl(GainControl.class);
gain.setGain(250);   // only once the camera reports STREAMING

Sources: FTC Docs · VisionPortal camera controls

2 Decimation too high for the distance

Decimation trades range for speed. Higher decimation runs faster but loses far-away tags.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Lower decimation when you need range. In one FTC test with a C920 and 2" tags: about 10 ft at decimation 1, 6 ft at 2, 4 ft at 3.
  2. You can switch decimation at runtime, low when far and higher when close.
Set decimation
aprilTag.setDecimation(2);   // lower = more range, fewer frames per second

Sources: FTC Docs · VisionPortal camera controls · GM0 · Vision

3 Camera lens isn't calibrated

Without lens calibration for your exact camera and resolution, tag distance and angle come out wrong even when tags are detected.

How to fix it 45 min

  1. Use a resolution the SDK has calibration for (it logs a warning when it does not).
  2. Otherwise, calibrate your camera and pass the lens intrinsics to the AprilTag processor.

Sources: FTC Docs · Configuring a webcam · GM0 · Vision

4 Camera on the wrong port or underpowered

Cameras drop out from ESD on the USB 2.0 port, from too many USB devices, or from loose cables.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Use the Control Hub's USB 3.0 port.
  2. FIRST recommends powering at most 2 cameras directly over USB. Use a powered USB hub for more.
  3. Add strain relief and a ferrite choke to the camera cable.
  4. Check the webcam name in the configuration matches your code (often "Webcam 1").

Sources: FTC Docs · Configuring a webcam · FTC Docs · Managing ESD · FTC Docs · Power management

5 Vision is eating the processor

A camera at high resolution with live preview and several processors can slow the whole robot down.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Turn off the live view for matches, and lower the camera resolution.
  2. Disable processors you are not using with setProcessorEnabled(..., false), or stop streaming when vision is not needed.

Sources: FTC Docs · VisionPortal CPU and bandwidth
